english.html: A pretext of marriage it truly was, for of lawful conjunction, Martin Guerre being alive, there could be none <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>: for several reasons, of which there are two principal ones. The first, that a woman cannot have two husbands <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>; nay, it is not credible that she should desire them <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>, unless it were in the country of the Medes, where the women are brought up in such an opinion that nothing more fortunate or honourable can befall them than for each to have several husbands: indeed, to have fewer than five seems to them a thing as it were ignominious, calamitous and wretched <sup class="mk" data-key="d">d</sup>. The second reason, that although there might have been a marriage, there was error in the person, which error hinders the will, and in consequence the marriage <sup class="mk" data-key="e">e</sup>, which takes its essence from the will and consent of the parties <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup>. It will perhaps be objected to me that between Jacob and Leah there was a marriage, although Jacob thought to espouse and lie with Rachel, for whom he had served Laban his father-in-law seven years — who nevertheless, on the wedding night, substituted for Jacob his elder daughter Leah in place of Rachel the younger <sup class="mk" data-key="g">g</sup>. But the answer is plain: that although at the beginning Jacob had not consented to Leah, nevertheless afterwards he received her as his wife, approving the substitution and the marriage, which suffices <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup>.

notes.citation: Decretum of Gratian, Part II, C. 34 q. 1 (the causa on the wife of a man taken captive who marries again), c. Cum in captivitate (chapter not verified)
notes.original: c. cum in captiuitate. xxxiiij. q j.
notes.gloss: The transcribers read priuitate/ptiuitate for the second half of the word divided across two margin lines; captiuitate either way. The same chapter is cited at annot-094 {d} as c. in captiuitate. Cited for the rule that no second marriage can stand while the first husband lives.
The paragraph contains the rule eadem duobus nupta esse non potest — the same woman cannot be married to two men; the swash P of the print is the paragraph sign.

notes.citation: Digest 23.3 (De iure dotium), the second law beginning Si mulier (fragment not identified)
notes.original: l. ſi mulier. la ij. D. de iur. dot.
notes.gloss: Several fragments of the title open Si mulier; Coras specifies "the second". The transcribers' iur- / iur. is the abbreviation iur[e], read with its point.

notes.original: Strabo au liure xi. de ſa Geographie.
notes.gloss: Strabo on the mountain peoples of Media: it is held honourable for a woman to have as many husbands as possible, and to have fewer than five is thought a calamity.

notes.citation: Decretum, C. 29 q. 1, c. 1 (Gratian's dictum on error of person)
notes.gloss: Error as to the person prevents consent and so the marriage; cited again at annot-097 {q} as c. j. § quod autem, xxix. q. j., and at annot-010 {h}.

notes.citation: Digest 50.17 (De diversis regulis iuris antiqui), l. Nuptias (D. 50.17.30, Ulpian); Decretum, C. 27 q. 2, c. Sufficiat (c. 2)
notes.original: l. nuptias. D. de reg. iur. c. ſufficiat. xxvij. q. ij.
notes.gloss: Nuptias non concubitus, sed consensus facit — it is consent, not intercourse, that makes a marriage; the canon (from Chrysostom) says the consent of the parties alone suffices according to the laws.
Laban substitutes Leah for Rachel. Chapter 27 is the deception of Isaac; the Jacob and Leah story is chapter 29, as the print itself has it at annot-081 {h} and annot-097 {ſ}.

lines: Pretexte de mariage, eſtoit il veritablement, car
de legitime conionction, viuant Martin Guerre, n'en
y pouuoit auoir {a}: par pluſieurs raiſons, deſquelles en
y a deux principales. La premiere, qu'vne femme ne
peut auoir deux maris {b}. voire n'eſt croyable qu'elle les
deſire {c}, ou fut au pays des Medes, où les femmes ſont
nourries à telle opinion, qu'il ne leur peut aduenir cho-
ſe plus heureuſe, ni honnorable, que d'auoir chacune
pluſieurs maris: voire d'en auoir moins de cinq leur
ſemble eſtre choſe comme ignominieuſe, calamiteuſe,
& miſerable {d}. La ſeconde raiſon, que bien qu'il y euſt
peu auoir mariage, il y auoit erreur en la perſonne, la-
quelle erreur empeſche la volonté, & en conſequent
le mariage {e}, qui prend ſon eſſence du vouloir, & con-
ſentement des parties {f}. On m'oppoſera peut eſtre,
qu'entre Iacob & Lea y eut mariage, bien que Iacob
penſaſt eſpouſer & coucher auec Rachel, pour laquel-
le il auoit ſerui ſept ans Laban ſon beau-pere: qui
neantmoins ſuppoſa le ſoir des nopces à Iacob ſa fille
aiſnée Lea, au lieu de Rachel puiſnee {g}. Mais la reſpon
ſe eſt claire, que iaçoit du commencement Iacob n'euſt
conſenti à Lea: toutesfois apres, il la receut pour fem
me, approuuant la ſuppoſition & le mariage, ce que
ſuffit {h}.

readings.reason: Bertrande is the name as Coras spells it everywhere; Berrrande is a misread of t as r.
ca|priuitate = captiuitate, the canon Coras cites again at annot-094 {d} as c. in captiuitate; ptiuitate is no word.
D. de iur. dot. = de iure dotium, the Digest title, each word abbreviated with a point; a hyphen (iur-|dot.) would make one word of two abbreviations.
Ti|mothee = Timothée, the epistle cited (1 Timothy 5); motheo gives no French or Latin form of the name.
